thread:
Leah (Sales): BetaClinic POC reporting partial traces in their Splunk dashboard. They also see many 429s from our forwarder. Can ops triage?

Ibrahim (SRE): Can you paste the raw forwarder log snippet and one example trace id? 429s -> likely ingest throttling or header loss.

Leah (Sales): Snippet: `2026-03-19T09:11:02Z INFO forwarder batch=7 size=96kb sink=splunk status=429 err="rate limit"`

Dana (Platform): Two quick checks: 1) Console -> Observability -> Exports shows export status? 2) Are they using direct HEC or our forwarder proxy? If forwarder, try buffered_mode=true.

Ravi (Solutions Eng): Also check if their ALB/WAF strips `traceparent`. If headers are removed, Splunk will not correlate. Ask them to curl our API with `-H "traceparent: 00-aaaa...-0000-01"` and share server logs.

Ibrahim (SRE): Short-term mitigation: enable forwarder.retry_with_backoff and increase buffer_size to 256kb. I can flip these in the POC config (5-10m).

Leah (Sales): They want fixes without touching infra approvals. Can we do the toggle from our side?

Ibrahim (SRE): Yes, we can enable client-side buffering and also turn on prefix-based sampling to keep dashboards useful while ingestion recovers. Both are config-only on our side.

Dana (Platform): If buffering doesn't restore full traces, schedule a 15-min forced sampling window (`tracing.force_sampling=true`) so every request emits spans. That will show if propagation or ingest is the root cause.

ops-bot: INFO Change requested: enable-forwarder-buffer + backoff by=Ibrahim ETA=7m

Leah (Sales): OK I'll ask BetaClinic for permission to apply buffering and run the forced-sample test if needed. Target: verify one full trace appears in Splunk within 60-90 minutes.

Ravi (Solutions Eng): I'll draft a one-page runbook for their Splunk admin: keep `traceparent`, enable indexer ack, avoid pipeline rewrite.

Leah (Sales): Thanks all — I'll update this thread with customer approval. :thumbsup:
